step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard depicts Enel's 2bit telemetry data architecture for smart meters (devices). In the acquisition tier, telemetry is retrieved either via EC2 instances (pull pattern) or sent via IoT Core with Greengrass on devices (push pattern). In the processing tier, data moves through SQS into either Elastic Beanstalk (EC2 instances running SQS daemon/microservices) or AWS Lambda (serverless POC). Microservices store metadata/state in DynamoDB and stream data via Kinesis to S3. Redshift queries S3 using Redshift Spectrum for BI/analytics.

edges.notes: EC2 connects to device to pull meter readings
EC2 forwards collected readings into SQS
Beanstalk instances fetch messages from SQS
Beanstalk microservice persists state/inventory to DynamoDB
Microservice pushes logs, metrics, and raw payloads to Kinesis
Firehose loads streamed data into S3 bucket
Redshift Spectrum queries data stored in S3
Device pushes telemetry via Greengrass to AWS IoT Core
IoT Core forwards data to SQS queue
Lambda writes processing results to DynamoDB
